title: SDK intake rubric for polyglot auth + streaming onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Create a repeatable intake rubric and prioritization pipeline for SDK and client library feature requests focused on language coverage, authentication patterns, and streaming ergonomics — with an explicit enterprise gating checklist. Background: Over the past 12 months we have seen many ad-hoc SDK requests (language ports, OAuth/KMS integrations, streaming helpers). This ticket formalizes how PMs should triage incoming asks, what signals drive prioritization, and the minimal engineering/design acceptance criteria for enterprise readiness. Scope: - Intake rubric covering: language demand, auth pattern alignment (OAuth2, mTLS, SSO/SAML, KMS), streaming UX & backpressure guarantees. - Triage workflow (customer -> Solutions -> PM -> Eng/design) with SLAs. - Prioritization signals and scoring weights. - Enterprise gating checklist (security, observability, SLA, packaging). - Deliverables: rubric doc, intake form template, prioritization spreadsheet, handoff playbook and a short pilot with two enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Published intake rubric in Confluence with examples for 3 scenarios: new language port, enterprise auth integration, streaming ergonomics fix
Intake form templates available in Drive and linked from Support/Solutions triage playbook
Prioritization spreadsheet with weighted scoring (business impact, engineering cost, customer footprint, security risk) and sample scores for 6 queued requests
Agreement with ENG and DX (docs) on minimal API ergonomic pattern for streaming clients
Pilot completed with two enterprise customers and documented feedback in the ticket comments

open_risks: Security: KMS integration patterns vary by customer; need clear guidelines to avoid ad-hoc implementations
Maintenance: Supporting 6+ language ports with unique packaging requirements could create long-term maintenance burden if we don't standardize adapters
Backward compatibility: Some large customers use a forked Python SDK; migration path must be low-friction
Observability: Need consistent telemetry hooks across SDKs to map costs and latency back to tokens/requests
tradeoffs_considered: Strike between providing idiomatic language SDKs vs. a single thin cross-language adapter: opted to prioritize adapter for streaming to reduce maintenance cost, while allowing idiomatic wrappers for stable languages (Python, JS, Go)
Security gating: delaying some convenience features (auto-KMS auth) to enforce security review vs. delivering faster MVPs for high-revenue customers
Packaging: publish minimal packaging for pilot vs. full platform distribution (pip/npm/ghcr) — pilot uses wheel and npm package only
pilot_plan: Select two enterprise customers (ACME Corp, IntegriBank) in collaboration with Solutions and CSM
Deliverables for pilot: adapter reference implementation for Python and JS, example mTLS and OAuth2 flows, streaming examples with backpressure guidance
Collect usage telemetry and qualitative feedback over 3 weeks
Iterate on adapter API based on pilot feedback and finalize acceptance criteria
